summary: One launch ran at HEAD f63f2171e after a fresh production build. FR-4 (a) to (f) hold on the week 1 home, the week 1 read-along page with a highlighted word, and the week 2 home, in th and en at 390x844: no game bar, one visible label (one copy in the accessibility snapshot), one 48 px logo, amber and brown chrome with 0 blue elements, the title at ratio 0.80 and centered, and a brown current word with white text at 7.09:1. Six browser items found real edge defects that no shipped title or default view reaches: B1 text zoom, B2 page zoom, B3 the 60-character title, B5 wide capitals, B6 the blocked logo, and the dark-scheme word edge. All six are non-blocking, and B4 (the shipped long titles) passes. Two items were not evaluated because of a harness defect: the label copy count (a script-text count error) and F14, the 403 page (the fixture left the loops part in draft, so the teacher route answered with the 404 view). No phone result is claimed.
nonblocking_findings: N1 [B1] ux-browser-review: at text-only zoom 200 percent (label font 28 px) on 320x568, the centered label spans x 44.6 to 275.4 (th) and x 47.5 to 272.5 (en), so its left end sits under the logo (x 16 to 64, higher z-index). The overlap is 19.4 x 44 px (th) and 16.5 x 44 px (en) on the cover and the band variants (4 of 4 cases). The no-zoom control at the same viewport has overlap 0. The first letters of the label are hidden. Captures: b1-*-textzoom200-*.png. Route: Green may anchor the label to the right of the logo (for example left 72 px at every width) in a later change.

N2 [B2] ux-browser-review: at page zoom 200 percent of a 390 or 320 phone (195x422 and 160x284 CSS px) the landscape block fires on a portrait view (max-height 500 matches). The page overflows sideways by 60 to 139 px, the label ends 3.5 to 41.4 px beyond the hero (the label has left 72 px and no wrap), and the plaque overlaps the logo by 9.4 x 23 px at 195 and 32.6 x 21 px at 160, and the label by 101 x 8 px and 66 x 6 px. The 195 px capture also shows the part tiles in a multi-column grid and the heading pill on two lines. The width is under the 320 px reflow floor of WCAG 1.4.10. This review did not compare the base, so the page overflow may pre-date Phase 2b. Captures: b2-*.png.

N3 [B3] ux-browser-review: a 60-character title at 568x320 wraps to two lines (font 20 px, plaque x 2 to 546, y 23 to 75) and covers the logo by 48 x 33 px and the label by 128 to 131 x 18 px. The first words of the title (Pip and Nan) are hidden under the logo and the label. This confirms the known adversarial N3 and Review C C2-F3. No shipped title (6 to 13 characters) reaches it, and AC-4.6 asks for plaque_overflow_px=0 and clipped_text=0 only. Captures: b3-*.png.

N4 [B4 result] ux-browser-review: the two longest shipped titles (Is It a Ball?, Unit 1 Review) at 568x320 and 844x390 in th and en, on the cover and the band variants: 16 of 16 cases hold one line and overlap 0 with the logo and the label. The plaque top sits 8 px above the label bottom (y 33 against 41), and the two boxes are 154 px or more apart sideways. The adversarial model of 40 against 41 does not match the build (plaque top y 33, label bottom y 41). This item is a pass.

N5 [B5] ux-browser-review: a title of 13 wide capitals (WWWWWWWWWWWWW) at 320x568 overflows the plaque: the text is 31 px (cover) and 42 px (band) wider than the plaque, clipped_text=1, and the page scrolls sideways by 19 px (cover) and 30 px (band) in th and en (4 of 4 cases). The font fit assumes 0.68 em for each character, and a capital W is wider. No shipped title is all capitals. Hardening choice for a later change. Captures: b5-*.png.

N6 [B6] ux-browser-review: with the logo request blocked, the alt text Storytime Advantage shows inside the 48 x 48 px box and is cut to about Storyti. The alt ink is #3b1d0a, which measures 2.36:1 against the fallback hero green #2b6a3a. On the light sky of the place picture the text reads, so the real contrast depends on the art. It shows only if the logo file fails to load. Captures: b6-*.png.

N7 [B7 dark, adversarial N1] ux-browser-review: with a forced dark scheme the current word is amber #fcd34d with brown text at 4.92:1 (the AC-4.9 pair holds), and the band behind it is rgb(192,136,96). The edge of the word against its band measures 2.10:1, under the 3:1 of WCAG 1.4.11. The capture shows a legible word. The app has no dark theme of its own, so only an OS dark scheme shows it. Captures: b7-*-dark-scheme-current-word.png.

N8 [Review C C3-F1 accepted] ux-browser-review: keyboard focus on a read-along sentence shows the two-tone ring (outline 3px solid white, shadow 6px brown #92400e) in th and en, and the ring encloses the whole sentence. A focused clip word (tabindex -1; the word I, a 7 x 48 px box) shows the same ring. In the capture the ring edge sits about 1 to 3 px from the comma of Hello, and from the letter a of am: it touches no neighbor box (neighbor boxes inside the 6 px reach: 0), but the ring is tight on a one-letter word. Under the sentence ring a small notch shows below the word I, because the 48 px word box is taller than the 45 px sentence box. Both are cosmetic. Captures: b7-*-focus-sentence.png, b7-*-focus-clip-word.png.

N9 [F14 not evaluated] ux-browser-review: the Review A nit F14 (does the 403 page show its heading text) was not decided in a browser. The harness fixture kept the shipped w01, whose loops part is draft. The route /th/teacher/2/1 therefore answered the 404 view (status 404) for the family session and for the teacher session, so the forbidden view never rendered. The gate fixture approves the loops part, and gate row 18 at 65b8325b0 read status 200 for the 403 page. Static evidence only: apps/storytime/messages/en.json and th.json hold teacherForbiddenHeading (This page is for teachers; the Thai text หน้านี้สำหรับครู), and teacher/forbidden.tsx renders it in an h1 of text-2xl. The teacher week and the teacher day screens (screen 6) were not evaluated for the same cause. A fix is one fixture line and one more launch. The orchestrator decides; Review A proposed to defer F14 to Phase 3.

N10 [harness defect] ux-browser-review: six FR-4 rows print FAIL with the reason b: label copies=2 and nothing else. The count used body.textContent, and that text includes the RSC payload script of the page, which holds the label string once more. The accessibility snapshots show one paragraph with the label on each screen: grep -c finds Level 2 once in p1-en-390-week1-home, p1-en-390-week1-readalong, and p1-en-390-week2-home (the th files show the Thai label once). The FAIL rows are a harness count error, not an app defect. The AC-4.2 copy count belongs to look-brand-chrome.test.tsx and gate row 15.

N11 [observation] ux-browser-review: the 404 view renders a Thai heading with an English line in both locales (the en view at /en/st/2/9 shows the Thai heading and the English sentence This page is not here). This review did not check whether the mix is the intended bilingual design of not-found-view.tsx. The Phase 2b change to that view is class strings only.
